In the Data For Good generative AI white paper, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint initially was calculated at 30 tonnes CO2eq based on direct energy consumption and carbon intensity of the electricity used. When extending the scope to include additional factors such as the consumption of other data center equipment (increasing energy consumption from 433 MWh to 690 MWh), the impact rose to 39.3 tonnes CO2eq. Further including the carbon footprint of manufacturing the servers and GPUs (considering a 6-year lifespan and estimated manufacturing impacts) increased the footprint to 50.5 tonnes CO2eq. Finally, when adding the phase of model development (tests, evaluations, corrections), which was estimated to add 73.32 tonnes CO2eq, the total full-scope estimated carbon footprint for BLOOM's training phase reached 123.82 tonnes CO2eq. 

Thus, the estimate increased from an initial 30 tonnes CO2eq to a comprehensive full-scope estimate of approximately 124 tonnes CO2eq, about four times higher than the initial calculation.
